title: Separate Takeout Scraps from Packaging
instruction: Put all the fries and chicken nuggets through the COMPOST opening. Put the checkered liner and the empty takeout container through the LANDFILL opening. Keep food off the table.
context: At a dining hall waste station, a diner empties leftover food into the compost bin and discards the packaging separately. A loose paper liner complicates the pour. Fries can catch in its folds, and tipping the box can send the liner into the compost along with the food.
setup: A 110 × 130 cm station tabletop is 74.75 cm above the floor. Two 27 × 29 cm openings each lead to a removable catch bin with a 33 × 35 cm interior and 25 cm depth. Each opening has a 12 mm rim and a 17 × 8.5 cm double-sided sign. Viewed from behind the robot, LANDFILL is on the left and COMPOST is on the right. For a physical setup, use a rigid laminate tabletop, plastic catch bins and printed signs on rigid stands. A closed, loose 22 g white polystyrene foam takeout box starts 24 cm forward of the robot frame origin on the centerline between the arms, with its hinge away from the robot. The rim measures 16.2 cm front to back by 23.5 cm across. The base is 4.4 cm deep and the lid is 3 cm high. The front tab on the lid has a 16 × 11 mm slot over a 9 mm raised catch on the box. A loose 24 × 17 cm checkered deli-paper liner covers the base, with its edges folded up the walls. It holds 16 potato fries (65 × 9 × 9 mm, 4 g each) and 3 breaded chicken nuggets (about 46 × 34 × 17 mm, 16 g each), totaling 112 g. The README gives the food layout, opening positions and reusable food props for physical trials.
scoring: Score the final state. Food separation earns up to 0.50 in proportion to the food mass in compost out of 112 g. If at most 11.2 g of food is in the landfill bin, the liner earns 0.20 for being completely inside that bin and the box earns 0.15 for being completely inside it and empty of food. The liner may remain in the empty box. Cleanup adds up to 0.15 in proportion to the fraction of food in compost and the unused fraction of a 20 g spill allowance. At 20 g of spills this component is zero. If the box or liner enters the compost catch bin, the food and cleanup components are both zero. A mixed dump into either bin earns zero. Count each type using 4 g per fry and 16 g per nugget, or weigh props matched to those piece masses. Use photos and a kitchen scale to check both catch bins, the box interior, both chutes, the tabletop and the floor. Food left in either chute counts as spilled. In simulation, a piece counts as binned when its center is within the inner walls and between the floor and opening of the catch bin. Food outside the box and catch bins and less than 3 cm above the tabletop counts as spilled. For packaging, simulation checks that the entire box and liner geometry is within the catch-bin volume, with 5 mm tolerance at its opening, walls and floor. Packaging crossing into the compost catch volume contaminates compost. Full credit requires all 112 g in clean compost, the empty box and liner in landfill and no spills. The simulator records four more seconds of the full-credit state before ending.
reset_notes: Empty both catch bins and clear the table and floor. Set the box back on its starting mark, line it with the checkered paper, fold the edges up and replace the 19 pieces in the README layout. Close the lid with its tab over the front catch.
fidelity: The foam box, fries and nuggets are rigid. The food is dry and does not stick. The liner has 63 rigid cells joined by soft hinges. It is 0.6 mm thick and weighs 9.45 g for simulation stability. Gaps can open between ribs. Each cell keeps its shape, so the liner bends at hinges without stretching or tearing. The lid uses a friction hinge. The modeled tab and catch have no snap force, and the box does not crush.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (recorded terminal state checked with the revised score). Scripted demo: 1.0.
